summary: Arcadian Insight — cascading failover and autoscaler feedback loop causing 5xx surge and streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-03-09 ~03:22 UTC Arcadian Insight began seeing a spike in 5xx errors and streaming connection resets for production traffic routed to us-east-1. The spike manifested as a cascading failover: requests were redirected from primary GPU pools to fallback pools, which then triggered localized autoscaler activity and caused repeated cold starts and transient errors.

Impact:
- Customer-facing inference calls returned 5xx for ~18 minutes during the worst window.
- Streaming sessions experienced truncated transcripts and repeated reconnect attempts for approximately 1,200 user sessions.
- Measured p99 generation latency increased from 120ms to 4.2s before mitigations.
- Estimated billing exposure: ~$9,800 due to retry amplification and cold starts (customer-facing).

Timeline (high level):
- 03:19 UTC - first elevated error rates observed by Redwood monitoring (api-gateway 5xx increase).
- 03:22 UTC - Arcadian CS reported customer-impacting failures via support channel and PagerDuty.
- 03:24 UTC - Automated routing kicked in, traffic diverted to fallback model variant (quantized).
- 03:26 UTC - Autoscaler began spinning new pods in fallback pool; observed overlapping scale events across multiple availability zones.
- 03:28-03:40 UTC - Rapid pod churn and transient kernel-selection errors caused repeated 5xx spikes and streaming disconnects.
- 03:41 UTC - SRE applied routing throttles and disabled aggressive fallback policy for Arcadian.
- 03:46 UTC - Hotfix deployed: increased warm pool buffer and adjusted autoscaler stabilization windows.
- 04:03 UTC - Error rates returned to baseline; continued monitoring and customer communication until 05:00 UTC.

Environment:
- Prod account: arcadian-prod (enterprise tenant).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Primary model: redwood-3.2 (non-quantized), fallback model: open-llama-13b-q4 (quantized).
- Dedicated routing policy: strict-affinity with dynamic fallback enabled.

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction path):
1) Replay Arcadian traffic profile captured from 03:18-03:30 UTC against a small cluster with identical routing policy.
2) Introduce a simulated GPU OOM/failure on primary pool to force failover.
3) Observe autoscaler policies across fallback pools and measure pod churn and kernel-selection errors.

Observed logs / snippets:
[03:25:12 UTC] api-gateway - ERROR - upstream response 502 (fallback-pool-az1) request_id=rc-9f7c
[03:27:04 UTC] runtime - WARN - kernel selection failed for model open-llama-13b-q4, reason: incompatible-kernel-for-seqlen
[03:27:27 UTC] autoscaler - INFO - scaling event start: pool=fallback-us-east-1-a target_replicas=6 current_replicas=1
[03:27:31 UTC] runtime - ERROR - stream reset by peer during kv-cache load request_id=rc-9f7c

Immediate mitigation applied:
- Disabled automatic fallback routing for Arcadian while we stabilized pools.
- Increased warm pool min_replicas for quantized variants by +3.
- Adjusted autoscaler stabilization window from 30s to 90s to prevent flip-flop scaling.
- Incremented per-tenant route throttle to reduce fanout on transient errors.

Customer-facing communications:
- 03:30 UTC: initial ack and high-level incident notice.
- 04:10 UTC: update describing mitigations and ETA for full recovery.
- 07:20 UTC: final incident summary and confirmation of compensatory billing credit offer.

Follow-up required:
- Post-incident RCA and runbook updates (see investigation_notes).
- Evaluate routing policy heuristics to avoid aggressive fallback when kernel mismatches are possible.
- Billing reconciliation and customer credit to be issued by Finance.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses and findings:
- Root cause appears to be interplay between aggressive fallback routing and autoscaler stabilization parameters. When primary pool briefly degraded (likely transient GPU driver hiccup), routing sent traffic to a quantized fallback variant. That variant required different kernel selection paths and had small warm pools; the autoscaler reacted to increased load with rapid scale-up. Overlapping scale events across AZs caused repeated cold starts and kernel selection failures, amplifying errors and triggering further fallback attempts (feedback loop).
- Logs show kernel-selection errors at the same time as scaling churn; kernel mismatch for quantized variant increased stream resets during KV cache initialization.
- No evidence of tenant quota exhaustion or auth issues. No config drift found in route definitions.

Actions taken by ENG/SRE:
- Patched routing controller to add a short-circuit protecting against immediate fallback when kernel_selection_errors > 5 for a given variant. (hotfix implemented: routing-controller v2.18.3)
- Increased warm pool targets for quantized variants and bumped autoscaler stabilization windows.
- Added metric: fallback_failure_rate per-tenant to monitor and alert earlier.

Related artifacts:
- Slack: #support-arcadian (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12A9GQ3)
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/arcadian/fallback-churn-2026-03-09
- PRs: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8421 (routing controller guard), github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8654 (warm pool adjustment), github.com/redwood/ops-docs/pull/129 (runbook updates)

resolution:
Hotfix and configuration changes resolved the immediate customer impact. Specific resolution items:
- Routing-controller guard deployed to prevent aggressive fallback during transient kernel errors.
- Warm pool minima increased for quantized variants (+3 replicas) and autoscaler stabilization windows extended to 90s.
- Temporary per-tenant throttles set for Arcadian while long-term heuristics are implemented.
- Billing credit issued to Arcadian; Finance ticket FIN-2026-003 created for reconciliation.

Follow-up work (owners and ETA):
- ENG-Runtime: Evaluate kernel compatibility checks and opportunistic warming (owner: Diego Morales, ETA: 2026-03-26).
- Platform: Implement heuristic-based fallback eligibility to avoid routing to models with known kernel mismatches (owner: Priya Desai, ETA: 2026-03-19).
- Support/CS: Proactive communication to other enterprise customers with similar routing profiles (owner: Evelyn Park, ETA: 2026-03-18).
- Postmortem doc and runbook published: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SUPPORT/pages/Arcadian+Followup+2026-03-09
